name: Five jailed participants in the 1966 St. Petersburg mural protest

prisoner.name: Joseph Wall
prisoner.description: Joseph "Jody" Wall was a Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee activist in St. Petersburg, Florida. On December 29, 1966, he helped Joseph Waller Jr., later known as Omali Yeshitela, remove a City Hall mural that protesters opposed for its racist depictions of Black people. Arrested and jailed, Wall remained in pretrial custody because he could not afford bail. A grand-larceny conviction brought three years of probation. On October 2, 1968, a Florida appeals court reversed his conviction and ordered a separate new trial; the subsequent outcome has not been established.

cases.charges: Grand larceny arising from the December 29, 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural protest; related municipal charges.
cases.convicted: Grand larceny: convicted May 1967; reversed and remanded for a separate new trial on October 2, 1968 (Wall v. State, 214 So. 2d 384). Subsequent outcome unverified.
cases.sentence: Three years of probation on the initial state conviction. Pretrial detention is documented: the six arrested protesters were transferred to the Pinellas County jail in downtown Clearwater on December 30, 1966. Wall remained unable to afford bail. Anita Richway Cutting's study cites an April 7, 1967 St. Petersburg Times report, 'Jailed 98 Days, Penniless Man Gets a Hearing'; this establishes an interim report of custody, not a final total or release date. The 1968 reversal ordered a new trial and was not an acquittal. The exact jail release and subsequent case disposition remain unverified.

prisoner.name: John Wesley Bryant
prisoner.description: John Wesley Bryant was a St. Petersburg member of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee arrested and jailed during the December 29, 1966 City Hall mural protest. His municipal trial resulted in a disorderly-conduct conviction, while a charge of destroying public property was dropped. He was one of four defendants acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. His detention preceded those verdicts; an exact release date has not been verified.

cases.charges: Grand larceny (state); disorderly conduct and destruction of public property (municipal), arising from the 1966 St. Petersburg mural protest.
cases.convicted: Acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. Municipal court: disorderly-conduct conviction January 30, 1967; destruction-of-public-property charge dropped.
cases.sentence: Held after arrest and transferred with the other five defendants to the Pinellas County jail in downtown Clearwater on December 30, 1966. Cutting reports a January 3, 1967 bond reduction that enabled release for defendants other than Wall, but does not establish Bryant's individual release day. At the January 30 municipal trial, sentencing for disorderly conduct was deferred pending a background check; the final individual sentence has not been verified. No state grand-larceny sentence: acquitted.

prisoner.name: Lemuel Green
prisoner.description: Lemuel Green was a Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee activist arrested and jailed during the December 29, 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural protest. Public defenders sought a reduction of bail or release for Green and Joseph Wall. Green was acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. A 2016 commemoration announcement named him as a posthumous honoree; his date of death has not been verified.

cases.charges: Grand larceny arising from the December 29, 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural protest; related municipal charges.
cases.convicted: Acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967; acquittal also identified in Wall v. State (1968). Separate municipal proceedings are described in Cutting's study.
cases.sentence: Pretrial custody included transfer to the Pinellas County jail in downtown Clearwater on December 30, 1966. Cutting reports a January 3, 1967 bond reduction enabling release for defendants other than Wall; Green's exact release day is unverified. The study describes thirty-day suspended sentences and probation for the four defendants tried municipally after Waller and Bryant. A suspended sentence is not thirty days of time served. No state grand-larceny sentence: acquitted.

prisoner.name: Tommy Williams
prisoner.description: Tommy Williams was a St. Petersburg Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee activist arrested and jailed during the December 29, 1966 City Hall mural protest. He was one of four defendants acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. In a later interview he recalled six months in county jail, but historian Anita Richway Cutting could not substantiate that duration. His detention is documented; its exact length and release date remain unverified.

cases.charges: Grand larceny arising from the December 29, 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural protest; related municipal charges.
cases.convicted: Acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. Separate municipal proceedings are described in Cutting's study.
cases.sentence: Held after arrest and transferred to the Pinellas County jail in downtown Clearwater on December 30, 1966. Cutting describes thirty-day suspended municipal sentences and probation for the four defendants tried after Waller and Bryant. Williams later recalled six months in county jail, but Cutting explicitly found no corroborating records and questioned that duration. Neither six months nor the suspended thirty days is entered as verified time served. No state grand-larceny sentence: acquitted. Exact release date unverified.

prisoner.name: Crawford Louis Jones
prisoner.description: Crawford Louis Jones was a St. Petersburg Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee activist arrested and jailed during the December 29, 1966 City Hall mural protest. He was one of four defendants acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. The historical record documents detention after arrest and separate municipal proceedings, but his exact release date has not been verified.

cases.charges: Grand larceny arising from the December 29, 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural protest; related municipal charges.
cases.convicted: Acquitted of grand larceny in May 1967. Separate municipal proceedings are described in Cutting's study.
cases.sentence: Held after arrest and transferred to the Pinellas County jail in downtown Clearwater on December 30, 1966. Cutting reports a January 3, 1967 bond reduction enabling release for defendants other than Wall, without an individual release day for Jones. The study describes thirty-day suspended sentences and probation for the four defendants tried municipally after Waller and Bryant. A suspended sentence is not thirty days of time served. No state grand-larceny sentence: acquitted.

sources.title: Anita Richway Cutting, From Joe Waller to Omali Yeshitela: How a Controversial Mural Changed a Man (2000)
sources.supports: Names of all six arrestees, including full names John Wesley Bryant and Crawford Louis Jones; initial detention; December 30 county-jail transfer; Wall's inability to make bail; Bryant's municipal outcome; suspended municipal sentences for the four other defendants; four state acquittals and Wall's probation sentence.
sources.qualification: Full mirrored thesis consulted. Its cited police reports, newspaper originals and interview recordings were not independently retrieved. Page 46 footnote 10 explicitly questions Williams's recalled six-month detention. Page 43 cites Carole Horn, Jailed 98 Days, Penniless Man Gets a Hearing, St. Petersburg Times, April 7, 1967, B11. Page 50 cites Alan Hopkins, Mural Case: 2 Guilty, 4 Innocent, May 5, 1967, B1. Do not treat publication dates as exact verdict/release dates.

sources.title: Wall v. State, 214 So. 2d 384 (Florida Second District Court of Appeal, October 2, 1968)
sources.supports: Wall's participation with Waller; Green among four acquitted co-defendants; reversal and remand for a separate new trial for Wall. Does not establish an acquittal, final release or post-remand outcome for Wall.

sources.title: Black community celebrates heroes, March 16, 2016
sources.supports: Names all six participants and their SNCC affiliation. Names Green as a posthumous honoree and Wall and Bryant as scheduled speakers. Used for identity and Green's deceased status, not exact death date or the article's erroneous January incident date.

sources.title: Yeshitela vs. the mural, January 5, 2017
sources.supports: December 29, 1966 incident, participant names and SNCC affiliation. Do not infer a birth date from Wall's reported age, which conflicts with other accounts.

editorial_notes: Only add missing people. Omali Yeshitela already exists; his historical case is separately prepared in batch 251. No existing biographies or cases are changed.

All five records describe former detention, not current custody. Leave release dates, birth/death dates, ages, photos and numeric custody totals unset when unverified. Do not interpret probation or suspended sentences as time served.
Thomas Williams is a conservative duplicate-review search variant only, not a verified alias or an assertion of Tommy's legal first name.

Do not populate website with a research citation: no verified personal/support site found. No inferred present-day prison address, institution association or coordinates for the historical downtown jail.

The appellate opinion inconsistently refers to six co-defendants while describing four acquittals and the two men involved in removal. Add only the six individually identified arrestees in the historical study and anniversary reporting, not a speculative seventh person.
